blocking.issue: The document requires every unit test to run under the race detector, and it builds with CGO_ENABLED=0 (G1, ADR-0001). It never says how these two fit together. On linux/amd64, linux/arm64 and windows/amd64, `go test -race` needs cgo and a C toolchain, and it stops with '-race requires cgo' when CGO_ENABLED=0. Turning cgo on for the race jobs fixes that, but then the tests run with the cgo DNS resolver and cgo `os/user`, not the pure-Go code that ships. So no pull-request stage runs the tests in the configuration that is actually released. Repository layout already allows this ('The race detector MAY enable cgo for test binaries'), but this document owns the pipelines and does not say so.
blocking.evidence: Unit and property tests: "Unit tests are hermetic: time, randomness and the State Store arrive as failure-injecting fakes, and tests run shuffled under the race detector." Test pyramid: "`pr-fast` builds the three binaries with `CGO_ENABLED=0` for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 ([tech stack](01-tech-stack-and-libraries.md#selection-criteria) gate G1 ...); shipped binaries come only from `release`."
blocking.fix: Add one sentence: 'Race jobs set CGO_ENABLED=1 for test binaries only, with the `netgo,osusergo` build tags; a second `pr-fast` job runs the same tests without -race under CGO_ENABLED=0, so the shipped configuration is tested.' To keep the length band, shorten the next sentence.

SM-6 is Planned (M2), and the Plugin kind, `ruralz plugin *` and the Plugin ABI suite are all Planned (M2). An M1 gate cannot benchmark a Plugin host that has not been built, and the M1 release gate 'every seed budget met' cannot pass while one seed has nothing to measure.

blocking.issue: The alloc/op gate has no baseline that any stage produces. The regression policy compares against 'the latest `main` result on the same hardware'. But the `main` stage runs only end-to-end and secret-leak tests (Figure 1), microbenchmarks run only in `pr-full` and `nightly`, and `pr-full` runs on shared general runners, where 'same hardware' cannot be guaranteed from one job to the next. A pull request's merge base can also be behind the latest `main`, so an unrelated regression that has already merged would be blamed on the pull request.
blocking.evidence: Regression policy: "against the default-branch baseline, the latest `main` result on the same hardware." Figure 1: "main: end-to-end on Docker Compose and kind, secret leak tests". Test pyramid: "| Benchmarks | ... | `pr-full`; `nightly` |". nightly jobs table: only the latency job runs on "Reference hardware, alone".
blocking.fix: Define the baseline for each gate. alloc/op: the same `pr-full` job benchmarks the merge base and the head on the same runner, interleaved, with at least 10 runs each (target). Macro latency: the previous `nightly` latency result on the reference hardware. Release: the release job re-runs the previous release's benchmarks on the same machine.

blocking.section: Plugin SDK and AI provider harnesses (AI provider mock)
blocking.issue: The 'Mid-stream error' case puts the commit point at the first chunk. The AI/LLM gateway puts it at the first content event, and it requires Provider Fallback for a stream error before content. An Anthropic stream always opens with `message_start`, which carries no content. So an `error` event after `message_start` but before any content block must fall back to the next candidate. This harness would assert the opposite and fail a correct implementation, or push implementers into the wrong behavior.
blocking.evidence: AI provider mock: "**Mid-stream error.** After the first chunk, the Node MUST NOT attempt Provider Fallback; it ends the stream with an `RZ-AI` error event." AI/LLM gateway, fallback matrix: "| Timeout or stream error before content | `perTryTimeout`, Anthropic `error`, Bedrock `modelStreamErrorException` | No | Yes | If exhausted |" and Figure 2: "AP-->>GW: status 200 and first content event / GW-->>C: response headers, now committed". Glossary: Provider Fallback "only before the response is committed".
blocking.fix: Replace the bullet with: '**Mid-stream error.** An error before the first content event (Anthropic `error` after `message_start`, Bedrock `modelStreamErrorException`) MUST cause Provider Fallback; after it, the Node ends the stream with `RZ-AI-009` and never falls back.'

Also note that at the seed of 30 allocations or fewer (hypothesis), a single added allocation (about 3.3%) already breaks the 3% (target) threshold.
